stem: The family of a client with advanced cancer and diagnosed cachexia says, 'If we can just make him eat enough calories, the muscle loss should reverse.' Which response by the nurse is most accurate?

options.A: Cachexia is a complex wasting syndrome that is not fully reversed by nutrition alone; care should address symptoms and medical contributors while using individualized nutrition support, often with a registered dietitian.
options.B: Cachexia is caused only by inadequate calorie intake, so increasing food intake is sufficient to reverse the syndrome in most clients.
options.C: Nutrition support has no role in cachexia, so dietary assessment and symptom-related eating problems should not be addressed.
options.D: Every client with cachexia should receive the same high-calorie meal plan regardless of appetite, symptoms, cancer type, or goals of care.

rationale: A is correct. NCI describes cancer cachexia as a wasting syndrome with loss of skeletal muscle and fat that, unlike simple malnutrition, cannot be reversed with nutrition support alone. Inflammation, metabolic changes, reduced intake, and symptom burden may contribute. NCI recommends multidisciplinary management and notes that registered dietitians can provide individualized nutrition counseling and strategies. B is incorrect because inadequate calories are not the sole mechanism and increased intake alone does not reliably reverse cachexia. C is incorrect because nutrition assessment and support remain clinically useful even though they are not sufficient by themselves. D is incorrect because nutrition intervention should be individualized rather than a single universal meal plan.
educational_objective: Differentiate cancer cachexia from simple inadequate intake and support individualized multidisciplinary management that includes, but is not limited to, dietitian-guided nutrition intervention.
source_organization: National Cancer Institute (NCI), National Institutes of Health
source_document_title: Cancer Cachexia; Nutrition in Cancer Care (PDQ®) — Health Professional Version; Nutrition During Cancer
source_locator: Cancer Cachexia — headings 'What is cancer cachexia?', 'What causes cancer cachexia?', and 'Ways to manage cancer cachexia'; Nutrition in Cancer Care (PDQ) — 'Anorexia and Cachexia', 'Nutrition Screening and Assessment', 'Methods of Nutrition Therapy', and 'Counseling by a registered dietitian'; Nutrition During Cancer — 'Nutrition screening and assessment during cancer treatment' and 'Ways to manage appetite loss, weight loss, and early satiety'.
source_claim_supported: Cancer cachexia is multifactorial and not reversed by nutrition support alone; individualized multidisciplinary care and registered-dietitian nutrition support remain appropriate.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Basic Care and Comfort — nutrition, feeding and comfort-related nursing interventions tailored to client needs and symptoms.
correction_summary: Rebuilt the source nutrition-plan item around the defining distinction between cancer cachexia and simple malnutrition, preventing the unsupported implication that calorie intake alone reverses the syndrome while retaining individualized dietitian-guided nutrition support.
audit_findings: NCI directly states that cancer cachexia cannot be reversed by nutrition support alone.
NCI supports individualized nutrition assessment and registered-dietitian counseling while addressing other contributors and symptoms.
No universal calorie target, supplement, feeding route, or drug is asserted.
Distractors isolate realistic misconceptions: calories alone, no role for nutrition, and one universal diet.
